proposals.relationship: Credits Société féodale with showing that collective sentiments and daily activities are significant historical objects.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2010 retrospective441 says the influence of Bloch’s book remained woven through his writing after reading it at the École normale supérieure. Named conceptual debt, not merely institutional affiliation; complete Bloch original unread. Preserves1939–1940 title as cited without implying an English translation appeared then.
primary_locators: Printed441, note15; breadth of research at442

proposals.relationship: Credits Ariès’s study of childhood and family life as an important model of historical inquiry.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2010 retrospective441 names L’enfant et la vie de famille dans la France d’Ancien Régime and calls it a masterpiece while acknowledging criticism of it. Admiration is not converted into agreement with every thesis or a formal teaching relation. Complete original book and criticisms unread.

proposals.relationship: Credits Febvre’s questions with directing his histories of fear, security and first communion.
proposals.evidence_note: Own signed Lettre6 p27 attributes initial fear inquiry to a1956 article; own2010 p440 answers a1952 book-review question about security and p446 recalls a suggestion to historicize first communion. These are separate prompts, not one reconstructed text or a claim of exclusive invention. Own2010 p441 additionally values Luther study. Underlying Febvre sources unread.

proposals.relationship: Guides Delumeau’s archival research on Rome and alum and provides a model of broad context and longue durée.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2010 pp436–437 credits Gaston Zeller’s thesis-topic advice and Braudel’s research guidance; Braudel is called primary adviser but contemporaneous formal degree-supervision restrictions are explicitly explained. Do not equate intellectual guidance with an inspected formal supervisor record.441–442 names Mediterranean as methodological example despite Braudel’s different interests; original books unread.

proposals.relationship: Invokes Duby as a model of writing for a broad public and an ally in interpreting the Reformations as a renewal of Christianization.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2010 p442 includes Duby among historians whose writing/research offered an example; p444 explicitly attributes the renewal interpretation to him. No particular Duby title is identified here, and underlying texts were not inspected. This is Delumeau’s stated appropriation, not formal mentorship or a claim that every medievalist shares his thesis.

proposals.relationship: Uses The Cult of Saints in discussing the persistence and transformation of religious practices under Christian forms.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2010 p444/n22 characterizes Brown as illustrating functions transferred from pagan gods to saints. This is Delumeau’s reading, not certification that Brown endorses Delumeau’s entire pagan-veneer thesis. Original Brown book unread; note22’s1980 bibliographic year is not separately certified or used to alter canonical chronology.

proposals.relationship: Adopts Le Goff’s description of Christendom around1500 as still nearly mission territory in arguing for late intensive Christianization.
proposals.evidence_note: Own1975 p58 says he thinks with LeGoff and cites Le christianisme médiéval, Histoire des religionsII,1972,p856 in note8. Underlying chapter unread; this does not make medieval Europe uniformly pagan or erase Delumeau’s later2010 p444 qualification of provocative wording. No inference from shared schooling or Annales membership.

proposals.relationship: Uses Vovelle’s testamentary research as the starting point for a methodological reflection on dechristianization.
proposals.evidence_note: Own1975 pp52–56 praises Piété baroque et déchristianisation1973 as a pioneering, rigorous and nuanced inquiry, then examines conclusions drawn from it. At58 he calls quantitative inquiry legitimate and indispensable for the institutional Christianity it measures. Original Vovelle book unread; praise is distinct from total methodological equivalence.

proposals.relationship: Distinguishes Vovelle’s quantitative history of religious practice from a qualitative history of different Christian models.
proposals.evidence_note: Own1975 pp56–60 explicitly calls this a methodological dialogue, says the chosen dossier is unassailable within its horizons and warns hasty readers against extrapolating religion’s complete disappearance. The comparison is undirected and not a claim Vovelle himself predicted Christianity’s death. Both approaches have distinct objects and can coexist; no manufactured personal quarrel.

proposals.relationship: As reported by Paillard, cautions that Freud’s negative critique of religion crosses disciplinary methods and documentary limits.
proposals.evidence_note: Fresh introductory17 is Bernard Paillard’s account of Delumeau’s interdisciplinary position, not a verbatim Delumeau answer.18–23 do not supply an additional direct Freud criticism. The named reported objection remains particular; no Freud title or universal rejection of psychology/psychoanalysis is invented, and original Freud works unread.
